stem: A client taking once-daily digoxin has a serum digoxin concentration drawn 2 hours after the morning dose. The client has no new symptoms. Which nursing interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: Use the result to guide the next dose because a 2-hour post-dose concentration is an appropriate routine sample for comparing with the therapeutic range.
options.B: Accept the result if it falls in the expected range because the absence of toxicity symptoms makes the timing of the serum sample clinically unimportant.
options.C: Repeat the concentration 24 hours after the dose because serum digoxin levels obtained earlier in the dosing interval are not useful for routine interpretation.
options.D: Interpret the result cautiously and obtain a properly timed concentration just before the next dose or at least 6 hours after the last dose, while considering the clinical picture.

rationale: Current DailyMed prescribing information directs clinicians to interpret serum digoxin concentrations in the overall clinical context and not use an isolated value alone to increase or decrease the dose. It also specifies that serum digoxin concentrations should be obtained just before the next scheduled dose or at least 6 hours after the last dose. A sample drawn 2 hours after dosing is therefore too early for routine therapeutic interpretation. A and B incorrectly treat the early result as directly actionable. C is unnecessarily restrictive because the label permits sampling at least 6 hours after the last dose rather than requiring a 24-hour interval.
educational_objective: Interpret digoxin levels according to both timing and clinical status: obtain the serum concentration just before the next dose or at least 6 hours after the prior dose and avoid dose changes based on an isolated improperly timed value.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine
source_locator: Dosage and Administration 2.5 Monitoring to Assess Safety, Efficacy, and Therapeutic Blood Levels: interpret serum digoxin concentration in the overall clinical context and do not use an isolated measurement alone to increase or decrease the dose; obtain serum digoxin concentrations just before the next scheduled dose or at least 6 hours after the last dose.
source_claim_supported: Routine digoxin concentrations should be drawn just before the next dose or at least 6 hours after the last dose and interpreted together with the client's clinical response rather than in isolation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed pp. 38–41: monitor therapeutic drug levels, evaluate client response to medications, identify adverse effects, and use medication-related assessment data to guide safe care.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — serum digoxin level timing and interpretation
correction_summary: Rebuilt all alternatives to remove absolute-word cueing and test realistic errors in interpreting an early post-dose serum digoxin concentration, while preserving the directly labeled sampling-time and clinical-correlation requirements.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Digoxin therapy — therapeutic drug monitoring and sample timing
audit_findings.stem: PASS — specifies once-daily dosing, a 2-hour post-dose sample, and absence of new symptoms, creating a focused interpretation task.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS as distractor — a serum level can inform dosing, but 2 hours after dosing is earlier than the labeled routine sampling window.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS as distractor — lack of symptoms is relevant clinical context but does not make an improperly timed concentration suitable for routine interpretation.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — waiting until just before the next dose is acceptable, but the statement incorrectly implies that sampling before 24 hours is not useful even though at least 6 hours is permitted.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS — directly matches both labeled requirements: proper timing and clinical-context interpretation; uniquely best.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — D is the only option that accurately incorporates both the minimum post-dose interval and clinical correlation.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — A and B overvalue the 2-hour level; C imposes an unsupported 24-hour requirement.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — no distractor contains the prior absolute-word pattern and all options are clinically plausible interpretations.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies includes therapeutic drug-level monitoring and medication-response evaluation.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether a symptom-free client could make the early sample acceptable or whether 24-hour sampling was mandatory; the current label explicitly requires just-before-next-dose or at least 6 hours after the prior dose and clinical-context interpretation, leaving D uniquely correct.
